content: Bismuth subsalicylate is an over-the-counter antacid that has been approved by the FDA for the treatment of diarrhea, heartburn, indigestion, nausea, and upset stomach. Common side effects include darkening of the stool and/or tongue, which are temporary and harmless. For adults and children aged 12 years and older, the recommended dosage is two tablets every 30 minutes to 1 hour as needed. Do not exceed 16 tablets (8 doses) in 24 hours. Children under 12 years of age should consult a doctor before use. It is advised to drink plenty of fluids to prevent dehydration associated with diarrhea. Each tablet contains less than 1 mg of sodium, 102 mg of salicylate, and 140 mg of calcium. The product should be stored away from excessive heat (above 104°F or 40°C) and should not be used if the packaging is damaged. Bismuth subsalicylate contains salicylate and should not be used by individuals allergic to salicylates (including aspirin) or those taking other salicylate products. It is contraindicated in individuals with bloody or black stools, ulcers, or bleeding problems. Children and teenagers recovering from chickenpox or flu-like symptoms should avoid this product due to the risk of Reye's syndrome, a rare but serious illness. If behavioral changes, nausea, or vomiting occur, consult a doctor immediately. Consult a doctor before use if you have a fever or mucus in the stool. Additionally, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you are taking medications for anticoagulation, diabetes, gout, or arthritis. Stop use and seek medical advice if symptoms worsen, ringing in the ears or hearing loss occurs, or diarrhea persists for more than two days. Pregnant or breastfeeding individuals should consult a healthcare professional before use. Keep the product out of reach of children, and in case of overdose, seek medical help or contact a Poison Control Center immediately. There is limited information regarding off-label uses, contraindications, drug interactions, and specific population guidance (e.g., pregnancy, nursing mothers, pediatric, geriatric, renal or hepatic impairment, gender, race, or immunocompromised patients). The mechanism of action, pharmacodynamics, pharmacokinetics, and nonclinical toxicology of bismuth subsalicylate are also not well-documented in the drug label. The active ingredient in each tablet is bismuth subsalicylate (262 mg), which includes 102 mg of total salicylate. Other ingredients include calcium carbonate, D&C Red 27 aluminum lake, flavoring agents, magnesium stearate, mannitol, pregelatinized starch, and saccharin sodium. The product should not be exposed to excessive heat and should be used only if the packaging is intact. There is no established interaction between alcohol and bismuth subsalicylate, but it is recommended to consult a doctor regarding the effects of alcohol consumption while taking this medication. The product is marketed under the brand name BISMATROL®.
